chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slaves of the people of the covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma), can I buy some of them? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Buy, when they have been endorsed with slavery.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for buying slaves from the Ahl al-Dhimma according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the condition of 'iqrar' (acknowledgment) for the validity of purchasing slaves from the Ahl al-Dhimma, reflecting the juristic principle that their enslavement status must be clearly established. This ruling underscores the importance of verifying legal status in commercial transactions within the Shia fiqh tradition, ensuring that the slave's condition is not merely assumed but confirmed by their own testimony or communal recognition.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a slave of the people under the responsibility (Ahl Al-Zimma), can I buy some of them? He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy, when they have been endorsed with the slavery’.
en.sarwar: 10. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the slaves of the taxpayers; if I can buy from them. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can buy them if they certify their slavery.’”
